So Fernández may travel up the M1 and M6 but the boos are likely to follow him after he scored and showboated in England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw land PFA Player of the Year awards
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers’ Association Player of the Year as Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw won the women’s award for the second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick to earn a Champions League return.

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals. He said: “It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it’s probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment.”

The Portugal international is the club’s first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10, and adds to his Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Shaw, who was also recognised by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women’s Player of the Year award for the second time. The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third consecutive Golden Boot and her maiden Women’s Super League title.

Arsenal’s Olivia Smith picked up the women’s PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool before continuing her form in the capital.

Manchester City’s Nico O’Reilly was named men’s PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze. The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City teammates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O’Reilly said: “I had a great season. I’m very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I’m over the moon how it turned out.”

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurriën Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford’s Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by teammates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year’s PFA Women’s Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo. Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United’s Jess Park were also included in the team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hayden Hackney, now of Everton, was named Championship PFA Players’ Player of the Year for his performances for defeated play-off finalists Middlesbrough.

Dom Ballard, who scored a jaw-dropping effort for new club Bristol City at the weekend, collected the League One award for a goal-laden season at Leyton Orient.

Swindon striker Aaron Drinan’s performances saw him collect the League Two award, while Lily Crosthwaite of Birmingham took the WSL2 player accolade.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football. Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as a player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland’s most capped performer having represented his country on 102 occasions. The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn’s Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup. Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

Sports.title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere.

Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.

Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.

Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.

West Ham’s clear out after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.

Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.

West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are plan to strengthen further.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out. The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.

Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts, and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is hauled off, mid-tantrum, at half-time by no-nonsense Ange Postecoglou - before team turn a 2-0 deficit into 3-2 win without him - in new challenge to his Saudi supremacy
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo is hauled off, mid-tantrum, at half-time by no-nonsense Ange Postecoglou - before team turn a 2-0 deficit into 3-2 win without him - in new challenge to his Saudi supremacy

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo's relationship with new Al Nassr boss Ange Postecoglou already appears to be under scrutiny just three matches into the season.

Al Nassr completed a remarkable comeback from two goals down to beat rivals Al Ettifaq 3-2 on Tuesday, but it was no thanks to Ronaldo, who earns an astronomical £488,000 a day, that the reigning champions claimed all three points.

The visitors appeared to be heading for defeat after enduring a disastrous first half which saw goalkeeper Bento sent off in the 12th minute for a challenge on former Fulham midfielder Mousa Dembele after rushing out of his box.

Al Ettifaq capitalised, with Ondrej Duda and Alvaro Medran finding the back of the net to take a two-goal lead into half-time.

Ronaldo, who was making his first start of the season following his return from the summer's World Cup, cut a frustrated figure as he headed towards the dressing room at the break.

The 41-year-old forward was seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel.

Postecoglou then boldly opted to remove Ronaldo before the start of the second half in what turned out to be an inspired move.

Ronaldo couldn't help but hide his frustration after enduring a disastrous first half which saw the reigning champions trail by two goals and reduced to 10 men

He was seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel at half-time

Postecoglou then boldly opted to remove Ronaldo before the start of the second half in what turned out to be an inspired move

Sadio Mane sparked the revival in the 74th minute before defender Abdulelah Al Amri levelled the match three minutes later. Mane then found the back of the net again in the 90th minute to complete the turnaround and seal victory.

Footage of the post-match celebrations showed no sign of Ronaldo celebrating the victory, while Postecoglou refused to indulge questions about his controversial call to drop the Portugal star after the match.

'I think there’s a bigger story today, and that is that ten men of Al Nassr were unbelievable. That's all you should write about today, everything else doesn't matter.

'It doesn't matter what team because if you see 10 men in those conditions for so long, 2-0 down to come back, that's the only story today.'

Controversy appears to have followed Ronaldo since his move to the Middle East in January 2023, following his public fallout with Manchester United.

At the beginning of the year Ronaldo went on strike over what he felt was a lack of financial backing of his Al Nassr compared to their title rivals Al Hilal. Both clubs are majority owned by The Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund.

Ronaldo was convinced that Al Hilal are getting preferential treatment, and he was particularly angry that they strengthened their squad by bringing in players such as his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema during the January window.

Saudi officials, meanwhile, were surprised that Ronaldo was unhappy given he is earning nearly £500,000 a day.

Footage of the post-match celebrations showed no sign of Ronaldo celebrating the victory

Ange Postecoglou:



“I think there’s a bigger story today, and that’s that the ten Al Nassr players put in an incredible performance. That’s all you should be writing about today.”

pic.twitter.com/7jSMfBAtqp — Al Nassr Zone (@TheNassrZone) August 26, 2026

Although Ronaldo is the face of the SPL, the league issued a statement firing back at the Portuguese star by reaffirming that he has no say on what happens at clubs outside of his own.

'The Saudi Pro League is structured around a simple principle: every club operates independently under the same rules,' they said.

'Clubs have their own boards, their own executives and their own football leadership. Decisions on recruitment, spending and strategy sit with those clubs, within a financial framework designed to ensure sustainability and competitive balance. That framework applies equally across the league.

'Cristiano has been fully engaged with Al Nassr since his arrival and has played an important role in the club's growth and ambition. Like any elite competitor, he wants to win. But no individual - however significant - determines decisions beyond their own club.'

Ronaldo claimed his first league title with Al Nassr last season.

Sports.title: LASK 5 CELTIC 1: Bhoys' Euro dream turns into a nightmare as Austrians let rip with five goals without reply
Sports.content:
LASK 5 CELTIC 1: Bhoys' Euro dream turns into a nightmare as Austrians let rip with five goals without reply

Austrians reach Champions League at Celtic's expense after 5-4 aggregate win

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Since embarking on their maiden European voyage in the old Inter-City Fairs Cup some 64 years ago, Celtic have scaled some dizzying heights and experienced some crushing lows.

Perhaps never before has the sense of sheer desolation felt quite as acute as it did when the final whistle signal sounded last night in northern Austria.

On an occasion when Martin O'Neill's side simply wilted before your eyes, a return ticket to the big stage was ripped up and the accompanying £40million in prize money slipped through the club's hands.

It was a catastrophic outcome – one which beggared belief after such a commanding display in Glasgow six days previously.

How could a side which was in such complete control of a tie at the midway point look so ramshackle and lost?

Celtic players are dejected in Austria as their Champions League bid disintegrates

It's much too easy to cite complacency on the players' part as the reason why Celtic again crashed out at this stage. They didn't initially play like a team that already believed the job was done. They just stopped playing.

Not since collapsing away to MTK Hungarian in 1963-64 had Celtic surrendered a three-goal first leg lead. The fallout from this will be nuclear.

For all the board were given some credit for lavishing £30million on four players, two of those – Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan – arrived too late in the window to take this match in their stride.

And where are the others which O'Neill evidently needed in the door sooner? The left-back, the holding midfielder that European football demands, the additional creative influence?

A club that's still in profit for this window didn't get its act together in good time. And, accordingly, it won't be returning to the big stage.

And so, the name of LASK joins that of AEK Athens, Cluj, Ferencvaros, Midtjylland, Kairat Almaty as sides to have knocked Celtic out in Champions League qualification in recent times.

You could lose one of those ties, maybe two, even if you are going about things the right way. When you chalk up six losses on the spin, you aren't behaving like a serious football club.

Few who watched this debacle unfold will ever have seen anything like it. It was scarcely believable.

When Callum McGregor found the net in 21 minutes, Celtic were four goals up on aggregate and contemplating what Thursday's draw in Monaco might bring.

While Benjamin Nygren's error allowed Moses Usor to level on the night before the break, there was no need to panic.

But that's exactly what unfolded. Auston Trusty's error played a part in Robert Ljubicic cutting the aggregate deficit to two.

Camilo Duran looks pained as Celtic suffer in Austria

More untidy defending then saw Samuel Adeniran net LASK's third and at that point Celtic were running about with their hair on fire.

With the Austrians completely dominant and managing 31 attempts in regulation time, the only wonder was that it took them until the 90th minute to square the tie with substitute Florian Flecker heading home a rebound.

Adeniran sealed an extraordinary comeback in extra-time following another elementary error and even had the luxury of having a penalty saved.

Celtic actually started the game fairly well. Baur's cross had a little too much on it for Kasper Hogh.

The German's interception sent Hogh in on goal. A poor execution ensured the keeper saved comfortably.

LASK were not shy at trying their luck from distance or shelling the box with crosses.

They were left with their heads in their hands when Xavier Mbuyamba failed to convert at the back post following a flick-on.

O'Neill's heart would have skipped a beat when Melayro Bogarde's strike took a deflection off McGregor and bounced off the upright.

Arriving just before the midway point in the first half, Celtic's opener owed everything to their pace and invention down the left flank.

Hyun-jun Yang played the ball back to Kieran Tierney and darted forward. Having taken the return ball, he bobbed and weaved while assessing his options.

LASK's Samuel Adeniran celebrates scoring his team's fifth goal against Celtic

Having correctly identified that McGregor was best placed to capitalise, he cut the ball back. The skipper's left-foot strike came off the outstretched leg of Andres Andrade and beat Lukas Jungwirth in goal.

Hogh looked like removing any lingering doubt soon after only for a nudge in his back to put him off.

With LASK looking increasingly frustrated, Adeniran pulled a shot wide of the far post then left one on Colby Donovan.

Celtic should have been coasting at half-time. Instead, LASK gave them something to worry about.

There was nothing wrong with Cameron Carter-Vickers' pass to Nygren. The Swede went blind with his attempted pass back.

Moses Usor could hardly believe his luck. A calm first-time finish gave the Austrians hope.

For O'Neill's players, it was a question of staying disciplined and sticking to their respective tasks at the outset of the second period.

Yet within three minutes, Trusty got himself done for pace and power on the left. LASK moved the ball into the central Robert Ljubicic.

The playmaker's shot from the edge of the box did fly through a thicket of legs. Still, Sinisalo was too easily beaten.

Ten minutes later, the unthinkable inched ever closer. A long punt up the park found Celtic's defence disjointed.

Donovan gave Ljubicic too much space to pick a pass to Adeniran. To that point in the tie, the American had played like his laces had been tied together. Not this time. His cushioned left-foot strike curled away from the outstretched arm of Sinisalo. Celtic were in trouble.

Reo Hatate and Seb Tounekti were introduced before Luke McCowan and Liam Scales joined them. Dane Murray later replaced the stricken Donovan.

Sinisalo did well to turn Sascha Horvath's deflected strike wide then watched Joao Viktor Tornich's point blank header flash wide.

When Adeniran's strike thumped the underside of the bar, the ball hit Sinisalo's back but stayed out. Celtic were riding their luck.

Celtic players call for offside after Florian Flecker's goal for LASK

O'Neill picked up a booking for venting his growing frustrations at the officials. Of greater concern was Kasper Jorgensen's shot which flew narrowly wide. Celtic were handing the ball as if it was a hot potato.

The clock had just struck 90 minutes when they conceded again. Finding himself in acres of space on the left, George Bello crossed. Sinisalo did brilliantly to prevent an initial header from finding the net but could do nothing as sub Florian Flecker nodded home the rebound.

All the momentum was with the Austrians in extra-time. Celtic got through the first period only to concede a fifth four minutes after the turnaround.

McCowan became the latest visiting player to make an enforced error when he won the ball on the edge of his own box and had his pocket picked. The ball was worked to Adeniran at the edge of the box who beat Sinisalo all too easily.

The Finn kept Celtic breathing by saving Adeniran's penalty after Hatate had felled Krystof Danek. It only prolonged the agony.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year after record-breaking season for Man United... and he's one of just TWO stars outside Arsenal and Man City in the Team of the Year
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has been named the PFA Players' Player of the Year after a landmark 2025-26 campaign in which the Manchester United captain broke the Premier League record for most assists in a single season.

Fernandes surpassed the previous mark of 20, jointly held by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, on the final day of the season when he set up Patrick Dorgu's header against Brighton to register his 21st assist of the campaign.

Fernandes has already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick by collecting the prestigious, player-voted award at Manchester's Opera House on Tuesday evening.

He was United's first to claim the PFA Players' Player of the Year since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

'Winning this, being voted by the ones that every week go out on the pitch against me, is something that makes me very proud,' he said.

'Because they've been there, they're playing against me, they've seen what I'm capable of doing, and for them to vote for me is something I'm very grateful for.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was crowned PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday

Fernandes, who attended with his wife Ana, was also named in the PFA Team of the Year

Fernandes had already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick on Tuesday evening

'It's always nice to see the name of the club in these kinds of awards, and obviously the players stand out with the club behind them. That's very important for us.

'I hope that from now on we can have even more players from our club having this kind of recognition, because it's also important and means that we're doing something very good.

'Individually, you want to have these accolades to show that your game is helping the team and that there are a lot of good things you've been doing to help them.'

The Portugal midfielder was the sole United player to have been named in the PFA's Premier League Team of the Year, and he is joined by Brentford's Igor Thiago as the only other non-Manchester City or Arsenal player in the side.

David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice all made up a heavily defensive Arsenal contingent, while Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland completed City's representation.

Mohamed Salah was named PFA Players' Player of the Year last year, but no Liverpool players made the cut this time.

O'Reilly also scooped the Men's Young Player of the Year award, beating team-mate Cherki as well as Max Dowman, Junior Kroupi, Kobbie Mainoo and Rio Ngumoha to the prize.

Elsewhere, Everton's Hayden Hackney was named the Championship Player of the Year after playing a key role in Middlesbrough's run to the play-off final in May. He signed for David Moyes' side in July after missing out on promotion with his boyhood club.

Nico O'Reilly (left) won the PFA Young Player, while Declan Rice was in the Team of the Year

Dom Ballard took home the League One title after a standout season for Leyton Orient while Swindon's Aaron Drinan won the League Two award.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award for the second time after also collecting it in 2024, becoming only the third player to win it twice after Lucy Bronze (2014 and 2017) and Fran Kirby (2018 and 2021).

Shaw was the WSL's Golden Boot winner last season, scoring 21 goals in 22 matches as she helped fire her team to the top-flight trophy for the first time in 10 years.

The other nominees for the top prize in the women's game were Manchester City team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Chelsea's Lauren James, Manchester United's Jess Park, Arsenal's Alessia Russo and Aston Villa's Kirsty Hanson.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award

The Premier League Team of the Year from the PFA Awards on Tuesday evening

PREMIER LEAGUE AND WSL TEAMS OF THE YEAR Premier League team of the year: David Raya (Arsenal); Jurrien Timber (Arsenal), William Saliba (Arsenal), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), Nico O'Reilly (Man City); Bruno Fernandes (Man United), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Rayan Cherki (Man City); Erling Haaland (Man City), Antoine Semenyo (Man City), Igor Thiago (Brentford). WSL team of the year: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea); Kerstin Casparij (Man City), Toko Koga (Tottenham), Ellie Carpenter (Chelsea), Emily Fox (Arsenal); Yui Hasegawa (Man City), Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal), Jess Park (Man United); Bunny Shaw (Man City), Alessia Russo (Arsenal), Lauren James (Chelsea).

Hannah Hampton, Kerstin Casparij, Toko Koga, Ellie Carpenter and Emily Fox made up the remainder of the PFA WSL Team of the Year.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith, the former most expensive transfer in women's history, scooped the Young Player of the Year award.

The 22-year-old Canada international became the first women's player to surpass the seven-figure barrier last summer when Arsenal signed her from Liverpool for £1 million, and had an impressive campaign, scoring five goals and recording three assists.

Sports.title: What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery... and the club's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi
Sports.content:
What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery... and the club's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Ollie Watkins' absence from the Aston Villa team at Brighton may have been the final chapter in a story that started more than 18 months ago.

The England forward spoke to his team-mates on Monday to explain his side of the story and is now expected to complete his acrimonious move to Al Hilal for around £50million.

Once Watkins had sat out the 4-0 defeat at the Amex, despite being Villa’s only fit striker, it created a rift between the player and the club, not to mention the fans, which was going to take work to heal. But while this row might have been handled differently by both sides, it has not come from a clear blue sky.

Daily Mail Sport looks at how we got here and what life after Watkins might look like...

The Arsenal bid

At some point last week, Watkins had a discussion with Villa manager Unai Emery, who left those talks believing the 30-year-old wanted to move to Al Hilal and was prepared to go to significant lengths to ensure the deal went through.

The striker did not train last week as he waited for Villa to accept a bid. The Saudi Pro League club did not make the required offer and once he understood Watkins would not be involved in the preparation work, Emery did not consider him for the Brighton match. Without the injured Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, strikerless Villa were hammered and Emery did nothing in his media appearances to protect Watkins, who was then targeted by fans online.

Unai Emery was in no mood to protect Ollie Watkins when his star striker was not available for the opening day at Brighton

Al Hilal, whose squad includes former Wolves captain Ruben Neves (furthest right) and Chelsea centre back Kalidou Koulibaly (second right) need to match Villa's £50m valuation

To understand it all, we must rewind to a sliding doors moment for Villa and Watkins — Boxing Day, 2024. In the previous three league games, Emery had picked the chaotic but brilliant Jhon Duran ahead of Watkins and the Colombian scored in all three.

Heading into that match at Newcastle, it looked as though Duran had become Emery’s No 1 striker. Villa knew Arsenal were chasing a forward and had an interest in Watkins, a boyhood Gunners fan.

Then Duran was given a straight red card at Newcastle and when he completed his ban, Emery did not feel his form or attitude merited a return to the team. Al Nassr offered £70m for Duran and Villa decided to cut their losses on a player who was proving difficult to manage.

Villa were unwilling to sell both forwards in the same window and Watkins was denied his dream move to Arsenal, whose offers never hit Villa’s £65m valuation. The forward was disappointed but Emery said: ‘Now we need him, like he needed Aston Villa.’

Emery has lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa this summer and wanted a few senior men to stick with him to build the new era.

Usually, the Spaniard does not stand in a player’s way if he wants to depart, but this one felt more personal.

Contrasting positions

Watkins is the top client at Two Touch, the agency run by former Arsenal youngster Paolo Vernazza. Watkins’ move to Al Hilal would likely be one of Two Touch’s biggest deals and Villa are unhappy with how Vernazza has handled it. Were Vernazza to have his time again, he might do things differently too. Daily Mail Sport has tried to contact the 46-year-old since Sunday, but he has yet to respond.

Jhon Duran was primed to be Villa's No1 striker 18 months ago before a red card at Newcastle

Aston Villa have already lost the likes of Youri Tielemans (left) and Morgan Rogers (right) this summer and Watkins (centre) may be next

Watkins is thought to earn a little more than £100,000-a-week at Villa, yet the salary proposed by Al Hilal is understood to be substantially more. Watkins has also seen Konsa, 28, join Arsenal for roughly the same sum Villa want from Al Hilal. Watkins turns 31 in December and if he believed Villa’s asking price was too high for a player his age, you could understand it. Not surprisingly, Villa saw it differently.

Under Emery, Watkins has developed into one of the best strikers in Europe. The manager has continuously backed him and was rewarded when he hit 12 goals in 13 games at the end of the season to force his way into England’s World Cup squad.

With two forwards injured, Emery needed Watkins at Brighton. No wonder he was ticking before the pre-match interviews. ‘Silence!’ hissed Emery when asked by Sky Sports’ Johnny Phillips about Watkins’ absence. With Emery, the less he says, often the angrier he is.

He looked a man on the edge at the Amex, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual, grew irritable with the opposing bench and stalked down the tunnel at full-time without shaking Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler’s hand. Emery and Hurzeler are not best mates, but the reaction was still telling.

What happens next?

A year ago, it looked as though Emi Martinez had played his final game for Villa. Desperate to move to Manchester United or Atletico Madrid, he was left out for a home defeat by Crystal Palace.

Emery looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual and grew irritable with the opposing bench

Watkins struck 12 goals in the final 13 games of last season to force his way into England's squad for the World Cup, where he scored in the warm-up against Costa Rica

The goalkeeper is still trying to get out, though he knuckled down last season and helped the club win the Europa League. With Watkins, though, that has looked tricky since Sunday.

Whatever the future holds, he has a huge job winning over Villa fans again. The reality is that there were signs last season that Watkins was in decline. A new deal may not have been the best thing for either party.

If Nicolas Jackson comes in, Villa have a striker with potential who can score goals. Emery likes him, having had him at Villarreal. Villa have also made an enquiry to Bayer Leverkusen for 20-year-old striker Christian Kofane. However, at this stage Leverkusen do not wish to sell.

Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they meet Arsenal at Villa Park on Monday.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling faces two years in jail after being charged with dangerous driving and possessing 'hippy crack' after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after his £270,000 Lamborghini crashed in May, it has been reported.

The former Premier League star, 31, who was arrested at the scene of the collision, faces two years in prison if convicted of the charges.

Police were called to the M3 in Hampshire on May 28 to reports of a Lamborghini swerving around the road just before 9am.

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail appeared to show the black luxury 4x4 veering across the three carriageways as other vehicles dodged out of the way.

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon - which is how people ingest laughing gas, also known as 'hippy crack'.

Minutes later, Sterling allegedly crashed the vehicle into the motorway barriers and was cuffed by Hampshire Police.

The force said he would not give a sample after his arrest - leading to a third charge of failing to supply a specimen.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman told The Sun: 'Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

Raheem Sterling has reportedly been charged with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide, and failing to supply a specimen

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail showed Starling's black Lamborghini M-way scraping the motorway central reservation, minutes before it crashed

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon, just visible as a dark circle above

'The charges come following a single-vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.'

They added that Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on September 15.

The charges mark a new low for Sterling, who left Chelsea in January after being dropped from their line-up and not playing since May 2024.

In February, he joined Dutch club Feyenoord Rotterdam, but that deal ended in summer and he has been without a club since - despite wanting to play.

The motorist who provided the dashcam footage of Sterling's sports car swerving told the Mail: 'I was in the middle lane and without warning a black Lamborghini pulled in front of me, forcing me to slow.

'I dropped back. I'm a driving instructor after all.

'The car turned back into the inside lane but the driver put his foot down and veered right across all three lanes and seemed to just avoid hitting the central reservation.

'It's a powerful car and he could have easily gone through the central reservation if he'd hit the accelerator.

'A van driver behind him was forced to brake and he then shot off again and turned back across three lanes again into the inside lane.

Sterling is engaged to long-term girlfriend Paige Milian (pictured)

Sterling, here playing for Feyenoord in February, has been without a team since the summer

'This was all caught on dashcam from 8.45am on Thursday. It was just before Junction 4a southbound on the M3.

'The motorist was all over the place but I had no idea it was Raheem Sterling until I saw that he'd been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving by the Minley Interchange.

'I like Raheem but as a driving instructor I'm very concerned.

'He could have easily caused himself - and others - a great deal of harm. He was very fortunate that he did not do so.'

Sterling's representatives declined to comment when contacted by the Daily Mail after the crash, but a source close to the player explained how he had had a hellish two years.

The source said: 'The psychological strain that has been put on him is immeasurable. Isolated. The second he touches a ball, being told he's a flop and he's finished. Mocked. Heckled.

'He moved to the Netherlands to escape and rediscover his love for the game but the negativity followed. It's been an extremely tough couple of years for him and this incident encompasses that.'

Sterling started his career at QPR but broke through at Liverpool as a teenager, before leaving Anfield for Manchester City in 2015, where he won ten major trophies, including the Premier League four times.

He played 82 times for the England senior team, with his last appearance in the 2-1 defeat by France in the quarter-finals of the 2022 World Cup.

However, since leaving City for Chelsea in a £50million deal in 2022 he has endured a torrid spell, which saw him exiled at Stamford Bridge before a failed loan spell with Arsenal and a move to Dutch giants Feyenoord, where he made just eight appearances with no goals.

Sports.title: 'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup
Sports.content:
'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

A statistic currently going around about Everton being the only club among the Football League's 92 not to have won a trophy, a title or promotion, or been relegated, since the turn of the century has contributed to a pessimism which made a gathering of the club’s faithful last Friday evening very welcome.

The occasion, at the Denbigh Castle pub, a legendary gathering place for Evertonians in central Liverpool, celebrated the former Everton captain Mike Lyons, whose life and career have been charted in a fine new book.

The aching sadness underlying an occasion in which Lyons' former team-mates took turns to relate stories of the indefatigable, generous and hugely talented team-mate they knew and loved, is that the man in question is struggling now and could not be there.

His daughter Francesca, who lives near Liverpool and calls him every day at the care home in Perth, Australia, where he is living with dementia, reminds him how cherished he is among fans. Lyons, 74, knew that the event was taking place and he knows about the book, The Man Who Bled Blue, a meticulously researched and beautifully written biography by the journalist and author Simon Hart. But his brain has frayed terribly. His family and friends have helped Hart piece together the life story.

He would certainly empathise with those 21st century fans who yearn for silverware – any silverware – and not least the League Cup, which sends the team to Preston, David Moyes’ old club, on Wednesday night. Everton were reigning English champions, four days away from contesting a European Cup quarter-final, when Lyons made his debut in March 1971.

Mick Lyons made 473 appearances for Everton in his 12 years on Merseyside, scoring 59 goals

‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses’

With Everton team-mates Martin Dobson (left) and Bob Latchford (right)

Yet his 11 years as an Everton player did not yield him a single honour. Liverpool won 15 in that time. By 1982, Lyons was on his way to Sheffield Wednesday, missing by a couple of years the start of the glorious era when Everton won the FA Cup and two titles.

Had Lyons been at Friday’s event, talk would inevitably have turned to the League Cup – and his huge role in Everton's marathon against Aston Villa in the 1977 final, won by Villa in a second replay at Old Trafford. It remains one of the greatest clashes in the tournament's history and was the closest Lyons ever came to silverware with Everton.

Evertonians still remember the intensity of his celebration when he scored an equaliser in front of the Stretford End in the second replay. ‘Michael was more animated there than at any other goal he scored,’ his brother, Joe, tells Hart in the book. (To his family, Lyons has always been ‘Michael.’) Fatefully, he was then asked to push up as a utility centre-forward as Everton chased a winner – it’s a strategy still known as ‘Doing a Mike Lyons’ among Evertonians – and a hole materialised at the back which Villa exploited to score a late winner. In the seclusion of the car on the way home, Lyons wept.

This story teaches us, among other things, that barren times can produce some of the greatest heroes, like Lyons, and that the League Cup can bring such indelible memories that Everton, who have not always fielded strong teams in recent times, should see it as an opportunity.

Hart relates how, despite the initial Wembley final not yielding a winner, the team still appeared on a planned open-bus tour of Liverpool for which vast crowds turned out. The first replay, a thrilling 1-1 draw in Sheffield rescued by a late Bob Latchford goal, would remain one of Lyons’ favourite nights of his career. He later described the noise made by Evertonians that night as ‘something I’ll always treasure. It embodied everything I’ve always felt for this club’.

The biography’s title, alongside an image of Lyons with a gashed face as he leaves the pitch after Everton’s 1980 FA Cup semi-final against West Ham – another one they lost – captures his contribution. His myriad cuts, blows and collisions form a backdrop to the book. ‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses.’

The book’s beauty also resides in its small details, capturing the boundless enthusiasm and often comic innocence which accompanied Lyons huge professionalism and work ethic.

He drove a club-issue Lada with his name emblazoned down the side. He eschewed the posh Liverpool hair salon which the players attended for their curly perms in favour of the work of team-mate Roger Kenyon’s wife Jackie, a hairdresser. Mrs Kenyon and Lyons’ wife Tricia were in such deep conversation in the Lyons’ kitchen that the perm solution was left in the Everton captain’s hair for too long. It was a catastrophe.

Shaking hands with Liverpool captain Emlyn Hughes ahead of the 1977 FA Cup semi-final at Maine Road

It is now 31 years since Everton last lifted a trophy, the 1995 FA Cup

The League Cup is the only major domestic trophy that Everton have never won, and it is time they rectified that point

You could have heard a pin drop in that Liverpool pub on Friday night when Francesca Lyons told the 100 or so people gathered that her father would have been humbled by all this attention. The consequences of his repeated heading of the ball are the same that so many old pros have had to face, full on, and Francesca has been an impressive advocate for football's need to do more for them.

There is a reason why the book’s subtitle is The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons. The Villa captain in the 1977 final was Chris Nicholl, who lived with the form of dementia caused by repeatedly heading footballs during his playing career, before he passed away in 2024.

But Friday evening was about the life-affirming qualities of a captain and player who, Francesca insisted, would not have had his life any other way. ‘He has always been so upbeat and fun,’ she said. ‘He would have probably laughed off all the attention because he’s always been so humble.’

Moyes, who also loves the bones of Everton, has a deep understanding of Lyons’ contribution. He and his long-time assistant Billy McKinlay paid him a visit during an Everton pre-season tour of Australia some time back. The League Cup remains a trophy Everton have never won. Lyons, who still watches the club’s games from Perth, would smile to see them finally lift the three-handled trophy next March, 50 years on from that legendary three-game marathon against Villa.

The Man Who Bled Blue: The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons by Simon Hart is published by Mount Vernon Publishing.

Sports.title: Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH

To catch up on all of yesterday's developments - including Aston Villa making contact with AC Milan over Rafael Leao - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

United youngster linked with Feyenoord

Manchester United forward Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Feyenoord.

The Dutch side, coached by Giovanni van Bronckhorst, want cover in case they lose a forward in the final stages of the window.

Obi Martin, a Denmark U21 international, had interest from Cologne earlier in the window.

Feyenoord would also offer Champions League football.

Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Dutch side Feyenoord

Forest close in on Delap deal

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea are closing on a £45million deal for Liam Delap.

Talks intensified on Monday following Chelsea's game at Fulham and a verbal agreement is in place for the 23-year-old to link up with Oliver Glasner's team.

He is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours.

Liam Delap is expected to undergo a Nottingham Forest medical in the next 24 hours

United complete Baleba deal

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

‘I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level,' said the 22-year-old, who has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford.

‘The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.’

For more on this story click HERE

Carlos Baleba with Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox

Gonzalez says goodbye to City ahead of £50m Newcastle move

Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez is travelling to the North East to finalise his £50m move to Newcastle United.

The 24-year-old Spaniard will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours.

Gonzalez said his farewells to City team-mates this morning and the deal is set to be £47m plus £3m in add-ons.

Nico Gonzalez will become Newcastle United's latest signing of the summer

City defender Kabore set for Wrexham medical

Manchester City defender Issa Kabore is due for a medical at Wrexham after they agreed a £2million fee. The 25-year-old spent last season on loan at Wrexham and wants to continue with the club as they attempt to take the next step up to the Premier League.

Kabore, who has 55 caps for Burkina Faso, has had eight loan spells since joining City from Mechelen in 2020.

Ipswich Town want £9m for Wrexham target Anis Mehmeti and Birmingham City are also interested.

Issa Kabore, pictured while on loan at Luton in 2024, is set to move to Wrexham

Bees still buzzing about Diouf

Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season.

West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford

Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre

Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre.

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league.

AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him .

Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City.

They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah.

Forest have also opened talks with Celta Vigo for right-back Javi Rueda.

Forest are discussing an £8m offer for the 25-year-old who joined Celta from Real Madrid in 2024.

Villa enquire over Kofane

Aston Villa have made an enquiry to Bayer Leverkusen for striker Christian Kofane.

As well as working on Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, Villa want another forward.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, they were rebuffed in an enquiry for Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta but have now turned to Kofane.

The 20-year-old's agent was in England earlier this summer talking to the likes of Everton and Arsenal.

However, at this stage Leverkusen do not wish to sell.

Wrexham close on £8m move

Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push.

Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million.

Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers.

Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old.

Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m.

They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

NATHAN SALT

Olympiacos in for Edson

Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan.

The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far.

Doncaster living the life O'Reilly

Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan.

A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe.

Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season

Tottenham seal Savinho deal

Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons.

Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City.

Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.'

De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity.

'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.'

Savinho signs on the dotted line for his move to Spurs

Pinnock in for Coventry medical

Ethan Pinnock is due to have his medical at Coventry today ahead of singing a three-year contract with an option to extend.

The promoted club agreed a £6m fee with Brentford for the 33-year-old defender yesterday.

Ethan Pinnock is set to bolster Frank Lampard's squad at Coventry

Chelsea in talks over Guiu exit

Napoli are continuing talks with Chelsea for Marc Guiu and defender Mamadou Sarr’s proposed loan to Sociedad is progressing. Chelsea have asked about Atalanta defensive prospect Honest Anahor.

Villa look at Leao deal

Aston Villa are exploring the finances of a deal for AC Milan's Rafael Leao.

Daily Mail Sport reported last night that the club had made contact over the winger, 27. Turkish giants Galatasaray remain in the mix for the Portuguese as well.

Rafael Leao in pre-season action against Chelsea

Bakwa off to Lille

Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa is joining Lille on loan.

The 23-year-old signed for Forest from Strasbourg last September in a deal worth £30million but has failed to have the desired impact.

He is due for a medical today and will play in the Champions League with Lille.

Dilane Bakwa is set to leave after just one season at the City Ground

City set to go back to Enzo

Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet.

But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night.

Sports.title: Leeds do the double over Nottingham Forest: Daniel Farke's side win at the City Ground for the second time in just FOUR days with Carabao Cup triumph - and Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for new boss Oliver Glasner
Sports.content:
Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for Nottingham Forest. Two games into Oliver Glasner’s reign at the City Ground, two defeats to Leeds United, and zero goals. He started three strikers and they still couldn’t score. And, so, for the second time in four days, Daniel Farke’s team came to town and took full advantage of a team still trying to find their new identity. First for three points on Saturday, now for a place in the League Cup third round. Daniel James was afforded the freedom of West Bridgford all evening and fittingly gave Leeds the lead before James Justin bundled in a second after a long throw caused chaos in the Forest box. Glasner’s side, once again, looked in desperate need of new blood. Thankfully, news emerged a few hours before kick-off that Forest had agreed a club-record fee of £45million, potentially rising to £50m, for the Chelsea striker. A remarkable whack for a player who scored just one Premier League goal last season and wasn’t even training with the first-team. Daniel James scored the opening goal as Leeds United won 2-0 at Nottingham Forest James Justin (right) scored the second as Leeds knocked Forest out of the Carabao Cup Delap is by no means the first budding talent to be chewed up and spat out by Chelsea and if Glasner can unleash the old-fashioned centre-forward that thrived at Ipswich, he would be just what they need. Glasner likes a physical focal point, as he had at Palace in Jean-Philippe Mateta, to hold it all together and bring team-mates around him into play as those around him attack with pace. ‘A frustrating night,’ said Glasner, who refused to comment on Delap’s impending arrival. ‘Last season told everyone what is needed, not just tonight. Nine months of relegation battle, losing maybe your top midfielder and now just six weeks together. The reality is no magician, no messiah, just hard work.’ That’s why Forest still look better when Chris Wood leading the line but he’s 35 in December and struggles with injury. He had the best chances of the night for Forest but couldn’t take any of them. A sensational last-ditch tackle from Joe Rodon denied him after a neat nutmeg of Nico Elvedi left him with just James Trafford to beat. Wood had another fine chance in the second half, too, but couldn’t beat Trafford from eight yards. Trafford is quickly starting to enjoy his football again. Two matches since his £40m move from Manchester City and two clean sheets. ‘It was a remarkable level of performance,’ said Leeds boss Farke. ‘Never in doubt, it was a fully deserved win. I saw how dominant we can be against really good sides.’ Forest boss Oliver Glasner has plenty to mull over after starting his reign with two defeats Carabao Cup R2 results: August 25 Cardiff City 1-2 Norwich City Doncaster Rovers 1-3 Middlesbrough Barnsley 3-2 Crewe Alexandra Blackburn Rovers 1-2 Sheffield United Blackpool 1-4 Lincoln City Cambridge United 0-1 Millwall Fletwood Town 4-0 Shrewsbury Town Ipswich Town 3-1 Leicester City Plymouth Argyle 2-4 Coventry City Sheffield Wednesday 0-2 Wolverhampton Wanderers Southampton 1-4 West Ham United Stevenage 0-3 Reading Stoke City 1-1 Hull City* (4-5 on penalties) Walsall 0-0 Leyton Orient* (5-6 on penalties) Watford 1-5 Peterborough Town Birmingham City 1-6 Brentford Nottingham Forest 0-2 Leeds United Forest, meanwhile, are still getting used to playing Glasner’s way and James repeatedly exploited the space behind wing-back Williams. James whipped one cross in to set up a glorious chance for Sean Longstaff, saw a shot of his own saved by Matz Sels. On 50 minutes, Williams bombed forward only for Arnaud Kalimuemdo to give the ball away and leave Forest exposed. Longstaff slipped in James who fired past Sels before Williams could get back. The puzzle of how to replace Elliot Anderson remains unsolved. Leeds’ second summed it all up as the ball bounced its way to the back post, Williams tried to clear it but couldn’t, almost put it into his own net, only for Justin and Lucas Nmecha to finally help it in. At least it was a more entertaining spectacle than four days ago. Neither side deserved to win that one. Leeds warranted every bit of their victory this time. The boos at full-time told you that.

Former Chelsea star Christopher Nkunku has secured a loan move to former club RB Leipzig. The former Chelsea ace had been linked with a move to Newcastle United this summer.

Instead, he chose to move back to Leipzig, the club he became a European star which earned him a big money move to Chelsea. The Frenchman was sold to AC Milan last summer for £32million.

"I could sense just how much the people in charge here still value me and how much trust they have in me. That's why Leipzig is exactly the right place for me to perform to my best.”

Sports.title: Match of the Day commentator fires back at Richard Keys in row over BBC programme
Sports.content:
Match of the Day commentator fires back at Richard Keys in row over BBC programme

Richard Keys has annoyed a Match of the Day commentator after sounding off about the BBC's iconic Premier League highlights programme on his new podcast

View 2 Images Richard Keys isn't a fan of Match of the Day (Image: YouTube/Keys & Gray Unleashed )

Richard Keys has been branded an "unemployable dinosaur" by a Match of the Day commentator after he slammed the BBC highlights programme.

‌



Keys and sidekick Andy Gray are embarking upon a new stage in their careers after leaving Qatar and their jobs with beIN SPORTS. The duo moved to the Middle East following their sacking by Sky Sports for making sexist comments in 2011, but are now back in England.

‌



After 13 years in Doha with beIN SPORTS, Keys and Gray have now entered the world of podcasting with a show called 'Keys & Gray Unleashed'. In the latest episode, Keys has voiced his opinion that the BBC's Premier League highlights show, Match of the Day, is unfit for purpose in the age of social media.

‌



He said: "When [Gary] Lineker left Match of the Day, there was a big fuss about who was going to present the programme going forward and my attitude then and remains 'who cares'? It doesn't matter. Match of the Day is a programme well past its sell by date. It was when Gary was presenting it. Who watches it?

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"By the time it goes to air everybody knows what's happened in the day. Highlights are available from 5.15 on most social media outlets. They even let commentators, in an eight-minute edit, do team news at the top. Why? What's the point of that?"

‌



He went on to lament the £390,000 to £394,999-a-year that Alan Shearer earned for his punditry role last year. "The BBC still think they cover football better than anyone else," he concluded before looking directly down the camera. "Not since 1992 guys."

Keys' not-so hot take has wound up commentator Dan O'Hagan, who has worked on Match of the Day, as well as other BBC sports highlights shows.

"So, this is to be their format then," O'Hagan wrote on X. "A pair of old, unemployable dinosaurs saying mildly controversial things for clicks. No better than the YouTubers or the s***-takes-for-likes influencers. Quite sad really, especially as Gray was genuinely the best co-commentator around."

‌



View 2 Images Mark Chapman, Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates took over as Match of the Day presenters in 2025 (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC / Charlie Clift)

Lineker presented Match of the Day from 1999 to 2025 before stepping down last summer. Last season saw Kelly Cates, Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan come in to share presenting duties.

There have been reports of tensions behind the scenes recently due to BBC director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski's plans to take the iconic programme in a different direction. Reports that Shearer had decided to reduce his appearances on the show to once-a-month have been rejected by the corporation.

‌



"The suggestion that Alan is reducing his Match of the Day appearances because of the director of sport is untrue," a spokesperson said.

A statement from Shearer read: “Cutting back my MOTD appearances is something we’ve been discussing for some time and purely so I can have some weekends back. I've always had a positive relationship with everyone at the BBC and that continues to be the case.”

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba earns Roy Keane comparison but grew up idolising another ex-Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba earns Roy Keane comparison but grew up idolising another ex-Man Utd star

Manchester United have invested in one of the best young midfielders in Europe in Carlos Baleba - now he must prove he can deliver on one of the most demanding stages of all

View 3 Images Carlos Baleba is now officially a Manchester United player (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Carlos Baleba has admitted he hates being compered to other footballers of his ilk.

‌



So he won't be impressed to learn that senior figures inside Manchester United believe the club has just signed someone who can have the same impact at Old Trafford as Roy Keane once did.

‌



That's quite a compliment - whether Baleba likes it or not. Because Keane remains one of United's all-time greats. One of the best midfielders of his generation. A rampaging enforcer who controlled games on his own. And won quite a few of them, too.

‌



Those in charge of recruitment at Old Trafford, including Christopher Vivell and head of senior scouting Kyle Macauley, have spent months watching Baleba's development on the south coast, while pouring over video footage of his performances.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And these two have seen qualities in the Cameroon international which remind them of Keane in his pomp. Why United have been persuaded to spend £70m on someone who Michael Carrick can go on to build his team around.

‌



A bundle of pace, power and stamina, complimented with excellent passing and dribbling skills and that rare ability to anticipate what is going to happen in a game's engine room.

Baleba grew up idolising Paul Pogba and has a long-held ambition to win the Ballon d'Or. He is not lacking in ambition.

View 3 Images Baleba has been compared to Man Utd legend Roy Keane (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



View 3 Images Carlos Baleba has completed a dream move to Manchester United (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"Everyone talking about you, singing your name? That just doesn't do it for me. It's not something that gets me running. I just prefer getting my head down and working on the pitch."

If Baleba proves a success at United, he won't have a choice in the matter when it comes to being hero worshipped and revered.

‌



He will have to accept his life has changed. "At the end of my career, I want to have an individual title, to play and mark a little bit of history like the great midfielders have done before," he went on. "And then win trophies, lots of trophies, with my club and my country."

United will now be keeping everything crossed he goes on to achieve his ambitions.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and laughing gas possession after motorway crash
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and laughing gas possession after motorway crash

Raheem Sterling is due in court next month to face charges of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling is without a club after playing for Feyenoord last season (Image: Gabriel Calvino Alonso/Getty Images)

Former England star Raheem Sterling has been charged following a crash on the motorway in May.

The 31-year-old, who is currently without a club, was arrested on May 28 following a collision on the M3 involving his black 4x4 Lamborghini. He is now due at Basingstoke magistrates court on September 15 to face three charges.

A Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.

Article continues below

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling is currently without a club (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported. Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.”

The ex-Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea forward had just finished his stint playing for Feyenoord at the time of the crash. After being frozen out of the first-team set-up, he terminated his contract with Chelsea in January in order to join the Dutch club.

Article continues below

He played under former Premier League striker Robin van Persie, but the short-term move didn't go to plan, with no goals or assists coming in his eight appearances for Feyenoord.

The four-time Premier League winner has spent the summer looking for a new club - a search which has so far proven unsuccessful. He has been keeping busy in the off-season by coaching at his own RS7 Academy.

Sports.title: Liverpool's dream end to transfer window as Bradley Barcola joins and £70m star signs
Sports.content:
Liverpool's dream end to transfer window as Bradley Barcola joins and £70m star signs

Liverpool could be set for a busy end to the summer transfer window with much work still to be done

View 4 Images Andoni Iraola will be hoping to add to his Liverpool squad (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool have less than a week until the September 1 transfer deadline as they look to drastically improve their squad. Andoni Iraola's side were held 2-2 by Newcastle United on the opening weekend of the Premier League.

‌



The game showed exactly what the Reds are lacking, namely direct pace in wide areas and stability in the midfield. With Liverpool understood to be in talks with PSG over a move for Bradley Barcola and Brighton for Yankuba Minteh, speed on the wings may not be too far away.

‌



However, the Reds' conundrum in midfield is an entirely different prospect. Here, Mirror Football takes a look at what Liverpool's dream end to the summer transfer window would look like.

‌



Sign Barcola

It's the transfer saga that seems to be showing no sign of ending. Paris Saint-Germain winger Barcola, 23, has been a top target for Liverpool this summer and the Reds must get the deal over the line.

The two clubs have been locked in negotiations for some time. Luis Enrique's side are said to be looking for a fee of around £130-£140million to part ways with the France international.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FC FACEBOOK PAGE! All the latest news and analysis from Anfield on the Liverpool Echo's dedicated LFC Facebook page

‌



While an agreement on a figure has yet to be thrashed out, it's understood that Barcola is open to joining Liverpool. The 23-year-old's desire could help facilitate a move, especially after the Champions League winners brought in Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts.

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola's move to Liverpool is sure to accelerate (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

It was claimed that a fee between £111m and £128m will be enough for the Reds to secure their long-awaited target. Rio Ngumoha, for all his gumption, was found lacking on the right wing against Newcastle on Sunday.

‌



The youngster looks a natural fit on the left instead, and with Barcola on the Reds' roster, he have healthy competition for the left flank and mentorship in the French star.

Bring in Mo Salah's replacement

It's been a long time coming, but could Minteh be Salah's replacement at Liverpool? Salah left the Reds this summer and it looked like movement for a right winger had stalled. However, Liverpool have had bids in the region of £50m and £60m rejected by the Seagulls for their star man.

The Gambian winger is thought to be valued at over £70m, with the Reds considering a third bid. Similarly to Barcola, while a fee hasn't yet been finalised between the clubs, Minteh is said to be keen on a move to Anfield and has already agreed personal terms, according to Fabrizio Romano.

‌



View 4 Images Yankuba Minteh shone for Brighton against the Reds last season (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images)

Minteh will give the Reds organic width, and while he is currently injured, he has built a reputation as an aggressive creator in his two seasons with Brighton. His goal record, just ten across two years, would need to improve but at only 22 years old, he has ample time to introduce that element into his game.

On the downside, Liverpool are reportedly willing to let Cody Gakpo leave, with Spurs and Manchester City interested, in order to finalise deals for Barcola and Minteh. While Gakpo has frustrated on occasion, his return of 51 goals since January 2023 is respectable and he will be sorely missed if he was to depart in the next few days.

‌



Recruit a midfielder

It's the one area of the pitch many Liverpool fans are screaming for to be addressed, and arguably the one that won't be. Not in this window, anyway.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan has many fans concerned that the Reds are leaving themselves short of top quality in the middle this season. Liverpool's engine room issues were laid bare against Newcastle.

Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai were often outnumbered and struggled to make up ground as the Magpies countered. Former Red Jamie Carragher claimed Iraola needs another midfielder with the physical attributes to accompany Gravenberch in the No. 6 position.

‌

It's believed Reds youngster Trey Nyoni will get a part to play this season, although the teenager didn't make it onto the pitch at St James' Park. Alexis Mac Allister did provide durability when he came on, but wasn't deemed good enough to start the game.

Who's available? Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton would be an ideal acquisition but the London club are in no mood to sell one of their prized assets with less than a week to go until the window closes.

Sports.title: Man Utd's dream end to transfer window with Lewis Hall U-turn and £40m deal struck
Sports.content:
Man Utd's dream end to transfer window with Lewis Hall U-turn and £40m deal struck

Manchester United have under a week to complete their summer transfer business

View 3 Images Manchester United are still extremely interested in Lewis Hall

Manchester United could offload a striker and sign their most desired target before the transfer window is over. Michael Carrick endured a nightmare start to the Premier League season after losing 2-0 to Hull City on Saturday.

‌



Despite this defeat, the United boss has insisted he saw positives and will not allow the team to be downtrodden by the result. He said: "It’s one game. It’s the first game of the season so it’s disappointing enough and it hurts, of course it does.

‌



"But it’s one game, it doesn’t change the whole course of the direction the team or the football club is going in. We’ll stay calm, stay in the bubble and focus on next week."

‌



Now, the manager will focus on bringing in new faces to boost the squad. Carlos Baleba is set to join from Brighton for a fee of £70million with the midfielder being sent for a medical at the weekend.

Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football has examined how United could add to Baleba's arrival and end the transfer window on a high.

Lewis Hall U-turn

It is no secret that United are huge admirers of Newcastle's Lewis Hall. The defender has been targeted by the Red Devils all summer but Magpies manager Matthias Jaissle emphasised that he is not planning to let Hall go.

‌



When United icon Peter Schmeichel asked if the full-back could head to Old Trafford, Jaissle exclaimed: "No chance! No chance!"

However, stranger things have happened in previous transfer windows. Newcastle fans will still be feeling the pain of the Alexander Isak saga last summer, where the once-beloved striker was ordered to train separately from the team amid claims of "broken promises" and "misleading" words.

The Swede eventually joined Liverpool for £125m after missing multiple Premier League matches and causing a transfer drama that is still talked about one year on. Hall is a totally different player to his ex-teammate and may not consider trying a stake-out to force a move to United.

However, he could see this as a viable option with Jaissle shutting down any speculation despite United still holding a keen interest in the 21-year-old. Hall is valued at around £34m by Transfermarkt, but a £60m price tag has already been mentioned.

‌



£40m deal done

View 3 Images Joshua Zirkzee could be on his way out (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee has been linked with a move away from United for some time. However, Carrick has no intentions of letting the Dutchman leave on the cheap.

The 25-year-old has attracted interest from Napoli, Aston Villa and Juventus. The Sun reports that United are demanding at least £40m before considering a permanent sale for the striker.

‌



Zirkzee could make a return to Serie A this summer after spending two seasons with Bologna before heading to Manchester. Football Italia claims that Juve have made enquiries with Napoli also keen.

However, both teams may need to make room in their squad before entertaining a move for Zirkzee. Villa were interested in the striker due to Ollie Watkins' impending exit to Saudi Arabia, but a move back to Italy could be more appealing to the 25-year-old.

With Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford all good options for Carrick, Zirkzee's Old Trafford exit could be on the horizon.
